key_insight: Motion 3-to-4 is a feed-forward pipeline that converts a single monocular video (optionally plus a 3D reference mesh) into a high-quality 4D dynamic object by explicitly separating static shape reconstruction from motion estimation, enabling temporally coherent 3D+time synthesis from limited data.
problem_solved: Addresses the ambiguity and data scarcity of recovering both geometry and time-varying motion from a single-view video, producing editable, temporally consistent 4D assets rather than per-frame or purely 2D outputs.
method: Decompose 4D synthesis into two complementary tasks: static 3D shape generation and dynamic motion reconstruction (per-frame deformation/pose) to reduce ambiguity.
Feed-forward architecture that accepts a monocular video and optional 3D reference mesh to produce a temporally coherent 4D representation without expensive per-scene optimization.
Leverage joint supervision from video observations and the reference mesh (when available) to produce high-fidelity geometry and consistent motion over time.
impact: Makes it practical to generate editable 4D (3D + time) assets from everyday monocular videos, lowering the bar for applications in AR/VR, animation, VFX, and data augmentation for downstream learning tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input monocular video (+ optional mesh) -> shape branch + motion branch -> 4D dynamic object output
